response.sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT category, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining, SUM(amount - spent) AS total FROM budget WHERE amount >= 75 GROUP BY category), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM cat) SELECT cat.category, cat.avg_remaining, cat.total, cat.total - overall.avg_total AS diff_above_average FROM cat, overall WHERE overall.avg_total IS NOT NULL AND cat.total > overall.avg_total

assumptions.assumption: The per-category total is SUM(amount - spent). Rows where spent (or amount) is NULL give a NULL difference, so SQL's SUM skips them. A category with no non-null differences has a NULL total.

The overall average is the plain average of the per-category totals. Categories with a NULL total are excluded from it, and every group counts equally. A NULL category value, if present, forms its own group.
